a4.cite: Finch, 'Several constants arising in statistical mechanics', arXiv:math/9810155v3 (1999; arXiv preprint read, publication not checked), Sec. 4 (Lenz-Ising model), table of the coefficients beta_k of beta(z) = lim (1/N) ln(1 + sum_r B(r) z^r) (B(r): even polygonal drawings with r bonds on the d-dimensional torus, z the activity; tanh^-1 z proportional to 1/T) as polynomials in d, quoted from Harris & Meir, Phys. Rev. A 36, 1840 (1987) (not fetched); PDF read. Evaluated at d = 2: beta_4 = (1/2) d(d - 1) = 1. Convention match: Finch's z is v = tanh K and beta(z) is g(v) = ln Z/N - ln 2 - 2 ln cosh K (Z = 2^N cosh^{2N}K sum_r B(r) v^r on the torus); exact rational, tol 1e-30
a4.independent_route: replicant's exact expansion of the Onsager double integral (series/ising2d.py: trigonometric moments in exact arithmetic, a different route from Finch's polygon counting); the exact 7 x 7 torus even-subgraph polynomial by a parity transfer matrix (series/ising2d.torus_free_energy_series, no Onsager integral): for odd L the even coefficients equal the bulk through v^(2L - 2) (an even-length wrapping cluster needs length >= 2L), so L = 7 reproduces a4 .. a12 exactly (tests/test_series.py::test_series_matches_exact_finite_lattice, which also checks this key against the 7 x 7 torus value)

v_c.cite: critical point v_c = tanh K_c = sqrt 2 - 1 of the square-lattice Ising model: Kramers & Wannier, Phys. Rev. 60, 252 (1941) (self-dual point) and Onsager, Phys. Rev. 65, 117 (1944) (not fetched: APS paywall, the ENS copy unreachable); read from Duminil-Copin, '100 years of the (critical) Ising model on the hypercubic lattice', arXiv:2208.00864v1 (2022), PDF read: Sec. 3.1 Eq. (3.3) and the text after it (beta_c = (1/2) ln(1 + sqrt 2), the self-dual point of tanh beta* = e^{-2 beta}), and Sec. 3.2 (the specific heat blows up at (1/2) log(1 + sqrt 2)); tanh((1/2) ln(1 + sqrt 2)) = sqrt 2 - 1. Concordant: Finch, arXiv:math/9810155v3, Sec. 4 (radius of convergence of the d = 2 series: sqrt 2 - 1 = 0.414213562373095049...). Value: sqrt 2 - 1 at 30 digits
v_c.independent_route: the leading coefficient of the operator recovered from the series by tools/annihilator (series/recognize.py): (u - 1)^2 (u + 1)^2 (u^2 - 6u + 1)^2, root u_c = 3 - 2 sqrt 2 = v_c^2 in exact Q(sqrt 2) arithmetic; the ratio method on the exact coefficients (tests/test_series.py)

alpha.cite: specific-heat exponent alpha = 0 (logarithmic divergence) of the square-lattice Ising model: Onsager, Phys. Rev. 65, 117 (1944) (not fetched: APS paywall, the ENS copy unreachable); read from secondary sources: Duminil-Copin, arXiv:2208.00864v1 (2022), Sec. 3.2 ('the specific heat C(beta) can easily be shown to blow up logarithmically as beta approaches (1/2) log(1 + sqrt 2)'), and Baxter, 'Some comments on developments in exact solutions in statistical mechanics since 1944', arXiv:1010.0710v3 (PDF read; journal reference not checked), Sec. 5.6 ('the Ising model, which has a logarithmic singularity in the specific heat'). Convention: C ~ |t|^-alpha with the logarithm as alpha = 0; the free energy carries (u - u_c)^2 ln|u - u_c|, i.e. the local exponent 2 - alpha = 2 with a logarithm
alpha.independent_route: the indicial equation and Frobenius recursion of the recovered operator at u_c in exact Q(sqrt 2) arithmetic (series/local.py: exponents 0, 2, 2 (a double root), the logarithm at 2, so 2 - alpha = 2); the ratio method on the exact coefficients (b_n ~ u_c^-n n^-3; tests/test_series.py)
